description:
Our team combines medical knowledge, engineering, mechatronics, space science, astrophysics, physics, creative design, presentation, and persuasion skills.

We’re passionate about innovation and interdisciplinary problem-solving, bringing different perspectives together to create impactful ideas.
We’re looking for a Game Developer to complete our skill set and turn our ideas into interactive experiences!
summary:
Earth, once resilient against countless disasters, is now collapsing due to wars, resource depletion, and a deadly radioactive alien invasion.

Dr. Anderson Schneider discovers a habitable planet 200 billion light-years away and plans to escape with his family. However, reaching it requires careful preparation.

Our Space Missions Game is an interactive educational experience where players complete progressively challenging space missions, manage resources, calculate costs, maintain spacecraft, and ensure crew health.

The game encourages independent research beyond in-game hints, enhancing players’ knowledge of space exploration.

Our prototype features four missions out of twelve, each containing multiple levels and challenges designed to prepare Anderson for his ultimate journey
details:
Earth is collapsing from wars, resource depletion and a radioactive alien invasion. Dr. Anderson Schneider discovers a habitable planet and plans to escape with his family. To get there, he must prepare a mission, and each task teaches him part of real space science.

Structure: The full game has 12 missions, and the prototype includes 4 of them. Chapter I has 5 levels: The Last Signal, The Supply Run, The Lost Sample, No One Left Behind and The Unknown World.

Gameplay:

  • The player walks through a space base in a top-down view, with a small radar minimap in the corner.
  • Each station (activated with the E key) opens a puzzle tied to a real mission.
  • Examples built so far: Object Scanner (drag an asteroid, a comet and a planet into place) and Sampling Arm (a timing challenge inspired by OSIRIS-REx sample collection).
  • After each puzzle, a declassified document shows real NASA data, followed by questions that connect the facts to Anderson’s own journey.

Learning idea: Players learn by making decisions, not by memorizing. In Chapter 3, for example, they compare the OSIRIS-REx and Stardust missions and choose a sampling site.

Current status: There is a 20-page Story Bible PDF covering the levels and gameplay, and a 7-slide presentation. The character and interface are planned for Unity.
